verdicts.title: Euler's explorations of extremal ellipses
verdicts.abstract_excerpt: In the 1770s, Euler wrote a series of papers (E563, E691 and E692) about finding the ellipse with minimal area or perimeter in the family of all ellipses passing through a fixed set of points. This is a translation of all three papers from the original Latin, together with a commentary which discusses Euler's results and an appendix which addresses a question from E691 which Euler left for others to consider.
verdicts.judge_reasoning: The abstract concerns Euler's 1770s papers on extremal ellipses passing through fixed points, which has no connection to clique complexes, Euler characteristic of simplicial complexes, or communication complexity.
